reason: The text is Ezekiel's famous 'Valley of Dry Bones' vision (Ezekiel 37:1-14), a prophetic passage about God's restoration of the nation of Israel. The passage contains no specific mention of elite or upper-class people, nor does it characterize any elite group unfavorably. The vision is entirely metaphorical, depicting dry bones representing the house of Israel collectively in despair and exile. While the people of Israel are described as having lost hope ('our bones are dry, our hope is lost, we are cut off'), this applies to the people generally during exile, not specifically to an elite class portrayed unfavorably.
